correct_answer_text: Durability
rationale: Durability guarantees that once a transaction commits, its effects persist through crashes/power loss, typically via write-ahead logging. ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

correct_answer_text: Azure SQL Managed Instance
rationale: Managed Instance provides near-100% SQL Server surface-area compatibility (SQL Agent, cross-DB queries, CLR, etc.), making it the default PaaS target for lift-and-shift.
scenario_anchor: American Airlines; Wolters Kluwer; Hexure (SQL MI migrations)

correct_answer_text: Eventual
rationale: Eventual consistency gives the lowest latency, highest availability and highest throughput, at the cost of no ordering guarantee. Strong is the opposite end of the spectrum.

correct_answer_text: A globally distributed NoSQL store; trade-off is consistency vs latency/availability
rationale: Global low-latency + flexible schema points to a distributed NoSQL document store (e.g. Cosmos DB). The key design decision is the consistency level, which trades off against latency and availability.
scenario_anchor: UnitedHealth Group (Cosmos DB for MongoDB, near-real-time patient data)

correct_answer_text: Native vector support in Azure SQL Database
rationale: Storing embeddings next to the operational relational data via native vector support avoids adding a separate service and keeps operational overhead low.
scenario_anchor: Dynamics 365 Business Central (native vectors in Azure SQL)

correct_answer_text: Heterogeneous = different engines; homogeneous = same engine
rationale: Heterogeneous migrations cross engines (Oracle to PostgreSQL) and require schema/code conversion; homogeneous migrations keep the same engine (SQL Server to Azure SQL) and are usually simpler.
scenario_anchor: PwC, Staples, Vale (Oracle to PostgreSQL)

correct_answer_text: SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA)
rationale: SSMA converts source schemas and procedural code (e.g. Oracle PL/SQL, Sybase) to Microsoft/Azure targets. DMA assesses SQL Server; DMS moves data; Azure Migrate discovers estates.
scenario_anchor: Northern Trust, LSEG (SSMA-based conversion)

correct_answer_text: Azure Database Migration Service (DMS)
rationale: DMS orchestrates the actual data movement (online/offline) into Azure database targets after schema conversion. SSMA/DMA are assessment/conversion tools.
scenario_anchor: PTC (PostgreSQL Migration Service)

correct_answer_text: Run an estate assessment first
rationale: Assessment (inventory, dependencies, compatibility, sizing) de-risks the migration and informs the right target and approach before any code or platform commitment.
scenario_anchor: PwC; UHNM (independent estate assessment & design validation)

correct_answer_text: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server with assisted conversion
rationale: PostgreSQL Flexible Server is the open-source target that preserves the Java microservices; SSMA/GenAI-assisted conversion plus validation minimises application disruption.
scenario_anchor: Staples (Oracle Exadata to PostgreSQL, GenAI-assisted conversion)

correct_answer_text: OLAP
rationale: OLAP is optimised for large aggregations, scans and historical analysis; OLTP is optimised for high-volume, low-latency single-row transactions.

correct_answer_text: A single, unified logical data lake for the tenant
rationale: OneLake is the tenant-wide, OneDrive-like logical data lake that underpins all Fabric workloads, providing a single copy of data accessible across engines.

correct_answer_text: Fabric Warehouse
rationale: The Warehouse supports full T-SQL DML and multi-table transactions on a distributed, multi-node engine. The Lakehouse SQL endpoint is read-only; Spark handles writes there.
scenario_anchor: East Sussex (Warehouse vs SQL Database vs Lakehouse decision)

correct_answer_text: It queries Delta tables in OneLake directly
rationale: Direct Lake reads Delta/Parquet in OneLake directly, giving import-like performance without scheduled import refresh or DirectQuery source translation.

correct_answer_text: Load to staging/heap first, then index and validate
rationale: Bulk-loading into a heap/staging table then applying indexes afterwards (and validating row counts and datatypes) is far faster than maintaining indexes during load.
scenario_anchor: East Sussex Fabric PoC (bulk-load tuning)

correct_answer_text: SSIS does not run natively in Fabric; re-implement in pipelines/notebooks
rationale: There is no native SSIS runtime in Fabric; ETL logic is rebuilt with Data Factory pipelines and/or notebooks (Python/Spark), sometimes re-engineering third-party components.
scenario_anchor: Sirona (SSIS & stored-proc migration to Fabric)

correct_answer_text: RPO (Recovery Point Objective)
rationale: RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss (how far back you may lose data). RTO defines the maximum acceptable downtime.

correct_answer_text: Automatic geo-failover with a read-write listener
rationale: Auto-failover groups fail a set of databases over to a secondary region and redirect app connections via listener endpoints, simplifying regional DR.
scenario_anchor: Nationstar, American Airlines (geo-DR)

correct_answer_text: The Fabric Capacity Metrics app
rationale: The Capacity Metrics app shows CU consumption, smoothing and throttling, so an SE can benchmark real workload cost before committing to an F-SKU size.
scenario_anchor: Sirona, East Sussex (capacity benchmarking with Metrics app/FUAM)

correct_answer_text: Active geo-replication / standby in a paired region with automated failover
rationale: Cross-region replication with automated failover is required to survive a full region loss with near-zero downtime and minimal data loss.
scenario_anchor: American Airlines (active-standby geo-replication)

correct_answer_text: Zone-redundant MI + auto-failover group to a paired region
rationale: Zone redundancy handles intra-region (datacentre) failures; an auto-failover group to a paired region handles regional DR. Together they meet mission-critical resilience.
scenario_anchor: Nationstar Mortgage (zone-redundant SQL MI, regional pairing)

correct_answer_text: A capacity/licensing transition (P-SKU to F-SKU)
rationale: The move from Premium P1 to Fabric F64 is chiefly a capacity/licensing transition; workspaces are reassigned to Fabric capacity and OneLake is adopted only as broader workloads warrant.
scenario_anchor: NHS Devon ICB (P-SKU to F-SKU migration)

correct_answer_text: Retrieve relevant context at query time and inject it into the prompt
rationale: RAG grounds an LLM by retrieving relevant context (often via vector search) and adding it to the prompt, improving accuracy without retraining the model.

correct_answer_text: Embeddings represent semantic meaning; nearest-neighbour search finds similar items
rationale: Embeddings are numeric vectors capturing meaning; similarity (nearest-neighbour) search retrieves the closest vectors, enabling semantic retrieval for RAG.

correct_answer_text: Azure SQL, PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Cosmos DB all support vectors
rationale: All three operational databases now offer native vector storage/search, so embeddings can live next to operational data rather than only in a dedicated vector store.
scenario_anchor: Business Central (Azure SQL), Repsol (Cosmos + PostgreSQL)

correct_answer_text: Cosmos DB knowledge graph + vector search (graph RAG)
rationale: J&J combined a Cosmos DB knowledge graph with vector embeddings/search and Azure OpenAI to ground AI over related structured and unstructured knowledge.
scenario_anchor: Johnson & Johnson (Cosmos AI Graph, graph RAG)

correct_answer_text: Mirror Cosmos into Fabric, model with medallion, expose a Data Agent
rationale: Fabric mirroring replicates Cosmos containers into OneLake; flattening into Bronze-Silver-Gold produces a curated model, and a Fabric Data Agent enables natural-language analytics.
scenario_anchor: iLending (Fabric mirroring of Cosmos DB, Data Agent)

correct_answer_text: One central fact table surrounded by dimension tables
rationale: A star schema places measurable facts in a central table linked to descriptive dimension tables; it is optimised for analytical queries and BI.

correct_answer_text: Bronze = raw, Silver = cleansed/conformed, Gold = curated business-ready
rationale: The medallion pattern progressively refines data quality: raw landing (Bronze), validated/conformed (Silver), and business-level aggregates/models (Gold).
scenario_anchor: East Sussex, iLending (medallion modelling)

correct_answer_text: Unified data governance: catalogue, classification, lineage, discovery
rationale: Purview delivers governance across the estate - data map/catalogue, sensitivity classification, lineage and discovery - underpinning compliance and trust.

correct_answer_text: OneLake shortcuts and mirroring
rationale: Shortcuts reference external data in place and mirroring replicates sources into OneLake, enabling interoperability with Snowflake/Iceberg without wholesale copies.
scenario_anchor: Bupa (OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, Iceberg)

correct_answer_text: Translate to business outcomes and analogies
rationale: SEs win technical decisions by mapping technology to business value, risk and cost for executives, reserving deep implementation detail for technical stakeholders.
scenario_anchor: Data SE role: consultative selling / trusted advisor
